description: Every client's Jamf Pro in one CLI: register each instance once, then find devices, check posture and patch status, and audit policies across all of them.

novel_features.name: Cross-instance device finder
novel_features.description: Find which client's Jamf Pro instance has a Mac, iPad or iPhone, by serial, name, username or email, across every registered instance at once.

novel_features.name: Fleet posture
novel_features.description: Per-client counts of stale check-ins, Macs below a macOS floor, FileVault off, firewall off and expiring MDM profiles, with Macs that inventory cannot fully judge reported as incomplete.

novel_features.name: Patch posture
novel_features.description: Patch titles behind latest and failing patch-policy installs (one patch_title row per client and title), plus failed managed OS updates (one os_updates row per client).

novel_features.name: Policy hygiene
novel_features.description: Flags policies that are disabled, can never run, have no scope, are expired, uncategorized, or point at a missing script or package.

novel_features.name: Instance registry
novel_features.description: Register each client's Jamf Pro instance once (server and API client id; its secret goes in JAMF_PRO_FLEET_SECRETS), then target it with --instance or report on all of them with the fleet commands.

novel_features.name: Service-plane health
novel_features.description: ADE and VPP token expiry, failed enrollment syncs, health check and Jamf Pro version spread for every client.

novel_features.name: Fan-out exec
novel_features.description: Run any read-only Jamf Pro or Classic API GET on every client instance and get one merged table with an instance column; credential fields are redacted and credential endpoints refused.

novel_features.name: App version exposure
novel_features.description: Which clients and computers have an installed application below a version floor.

novel_features.name: Baseline drift
novel_features.description: Compare every client instance against a golden instance: scripts by content, packages, policies, profiles, extension attributes and smart groups.
